findings.claim: The change alters the decimal wire format, which the requirement does not ask for. `DecimalFormatter.Serialize` now passes `new StandardFormat('F')` to `Utf8Formatter.TryFormat`. With no precision, 'F' rounds to 2 decimal places, whereas the previous default 'G' kept the full value. So 1.2345m is written as "1.23" and 0.001m as "0.00", silently losing data on round-trip. The requirement covers code-coverage attributes on generated code only.

receipt_plan.detail: Build MessagePack at base and at head. Run MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<decimal>(1.2345m), Serialize(0.001m) and Serialize(-12345.6789m) with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard on each build and compare the bytes. Base should emit fixstr "1.2345" and head "1.23". Then deserialize head's bytes and assert the value differs from the input.

findings.claim: Requirement: "All generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage". Every emitted attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get no attribute at all. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+ and applies to classes. The derived criterion only permits conditional emission where the attribute does not exist, and ledger L12 says to follow the requirement. These are among the most common consumer targets, and the README addition documents the gap rather than closing it.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2297NetStandardCoverageTests: run the generator with the NETSTANDARD2_0 (and separately NETFRAMEWORK) preprocessor symbol against net8.0 references, where the attribute exists. Assert every generated class, or a type containing it, carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. Expected to fail on head. The same guard appears in ResolverTemplate.tt, CompositeResolverTemplate.tt, EnumTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt and StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Emit [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] unconditionally, with no setting. The change does this: every template (formatter, string-key formatter, enum, union, resolver, composite resolver and its nested helper classes) writes the attribute, and no option or attribute property controls it.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Emit the attribute by default but offer an opt-out setting, which the requirement says would be fine. Add a bool property such as `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` (default true) to GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute or GeneratorOptions, read it in the generator's option parsing, and have each template write the `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` line only when it is true.
